# The drag sensors keep their pressed element after a click that never became a drag

## Context

Found by #19174's first headless film replay (2026-09-24 15:23Z, `WorkstationFilmTourNL.spec.mjs -g 'under autoGates'`, own bridge): the new `resize` cue, the first `InteractionService#driveDrag` of the film, ran right after the rail beat's clicks and was refused before any input:

```
film-resize[0] host step settlement failed: resize: the drive failed in phase 'busy': MOUSE_SENSOR_BUSY — the source window Mouse sensor is already engaged
```

No drag was in flight. The rail beat had clicked a tab button — a `neo-draggable` sort-zone item — and released it 60 ms later, before the sensor's 100 ms delay could arm anything. The sensor still reported a pressed element.

## The Problem

`Neo.main.draggable.sensor.Mouse#endGesture` (`src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs:227-257`) releases the physical gesture — the timers, the selection guard, the move/up listeners — but resets `currentElement`, `dragging` and `startEvent` **only inside `if (me.dragging)`**. A press on a drag target that ends before the delay + distance threshold (every ordinary click on a tab, a card, a splitter) leaves `currentElement` and `startEvent` pointing at the released node until the next mousedown overwrites them. `Neo.main.draggable.sensor.Touch#onTouchEnd` (`src/main/draggable/sensor/Touch.mjs:104-146`) has the identical shape.

The sensor's own next press overwrites the stale fields, so the sensor itself does not misbehave. The consumer that reads them does: `Neo.main.addon.EventSimulator#driveDrag` (`src/main/addon/EventSimulator.mjs:343`) refuses with `MOUSE_SENSOR_BUSY` when `sensor.currentElement || sensor.dragging` — the right predicate for "engaged", answered by state the sensor never cleared. Every consumer of the drive inherits it: the Neural Link's `drive_drag` tool refuses after the user (or any prior synthetic click) pressed a draggable in that window; `test/playwright/e2e/core/SplitterLiveResizeNL.spec.mjs` passes only because nothing is clicked before its drive.

## The Architectural Reality

- The Mouse sensor's press → release bracket is documented at `Mouse.mjs:148-171`: the guard and the listeners bracket the PHYSICAL gesture, released in `endGesture` on mouseup or on the move stream observing the primary button gone. The pressed element belongs to that same bracket; it is the only field the release forgets.
- `sensor/Base.mjs:19` declares `currentElement: null` as the idle state; `DragDrop` reads no sensor field, `EventSimulator#resolveMouseSensor` (`:239`) hands the live sensor to the busy check.
- Witness surfaces: `test/playwright/unit/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.spec.mjs` drives trusted-shaped events through an `EventTarget` document per sensor (the selection-guard terminal contract, `:129-240`); `test/playwright/unit/main/addon/EventSimulator.spec.mjs:278` pins the busy refusal on a sensor whose `currentElement` is set.

## The Fix

`endGesture` (Mouse) and `onTouchEnd` (Touch) reset `currentElement`, `startEvent` and `mouseDownTime`/`pageX`/`pageY` for every release, keeping the `dragging` branch for the `drag:end` trigger and the drag-only listeners. Two unit arms in the sensor spec: a pre-threshold release leaves no pressed element (`currentElement`/`startEvent` null, and a following `driveDrag` busy predicate reads idle), and the mid-drag release keeps emitting exactly one `drag:end` (the existing arm stays green). The `EventSimulator` busy predicate is unchanged: it was reading truthfully.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A mousedown on a drag target followed by a mouseup before the delay + distance threshold leaves the Mouse sensor idle: `currentElement`, `startEvent` null; the existing terminal-contract arms stay green.
- [ ] AC-2 The Touch sensor's `onTouchEnd` resets the same fields on every release.
- [ ] AC-3 `EventSimulator#driveDrag` after such a click reports no `MOUSE_SENSOR_BUSY` — pinned by the sensor arm reading the busy predicate's inputs, and by #19174's film replay (the rail beat's clicks precede the resize drive) going green at its PR head with this fix merged.

## Out of Scope

The busy predicate's shape, the sensor's delay and distance thresholds, and the `neo-drag-active` guard (#17883).

* fix(workstation): the resize receipt fails closed on its live-preview and one-commit proofs (#19174)

Euclid's R1: the preview proof was a fixed-clock sample that could precede the drive's mousedown or straddle the terminal, and applied never required it. The proof is now an observed condition — a pane box that moved while the committed document stood on both sides of the read and no terminal had landed — sampled through the cursor walk and then polled until the drive settles; applied requires that sample, exactly one accepted terminal and the requested vector. Four negative controls: a late-starting prelude is waited out, a drive that commits without a preview fails closed, a box read that lands after the release cannot pass as a preview, a second terminal fails the one-commit contract."
